publish_control.merge_policy_note: Committed, not merged. The deltas name their canonical destinations and do not reach them here. Merge happens at Phase 7.5 after the PR lands, so a canonical document only moves once the change is real — a delta merged at design time would make the baseline describe a system nobody has built.

00-overview.md.note: The only original content in the package. Everything else has a canonical destination elsewhere and exists here as a diff.

additive/.reason: Additive by nature. A journey map is a record of this cycle's design thinking, not an amendment to a standing document.

no_duplicate_authorship_check.note: Every file in deltas/ names exactly one canonical destination, and no two files name the same one. Nothing in the package restates content that lives elsewhere — the design is composed rather than duplicated, which is what makes drift structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

viewpoint_assertion_table.gate_note: All four viewpoints assert DELTA, which is unusual and is what Cycle 1 looks like — the first cycle touches everything. The gate blocks on an OMITTED viewpoint, not on a NONE: a NONE with a stated reason passes and silence fails, because an omission is indistinguishable from an oversight. Three of the four component-level NONE assertions in the APPLICATION row exist for exactly that reason.

blocking.detail: The integration delta is structural and propagates a new external edge to foundational-solution-architecture.md. The platform delta provisions the egress path that edge needs. Neither can merge until the ADR is approved, and the platform IaC is committed but deliberately not applied.
blocking.note: The other 12 files are independently mergeable in principle. They are held together anyway: merging the application and data halves of a cycle whose integration half is unapproved would leave a component HLD describing a call the architecture has not authorised.
